summary.text: The Andes are the world's longest continental mountain range, a continuous highland along the western edge of South America.
They formed as oceanic crust was subducted beneath the South American Plate while the Nazca and South American plates converged.
Their rise cast a rain shadow that left parts of the subduction zone short of sediment, which sped up uplift along the coast.

facts.label: Farthest from Earth's center
facts.value: The peak of Chimborazo in Ecuador

items.prompt: Chimborazo in Ecuador is far from the tallest mountain above sea level, yet its summit is farther from Earth's center than any other point. Why?

options.label: Earth's spin makes it bulge at the equator
It is secretly taller than Everest
It sits on top of a rising hotspot
The crust under it is thickest on Earth

items.explain: Earth's rotation makes it bulge at the equator, so a peak near the equator sits farther out from the center.

items.prompt: What has mainly pushed the Andes upward?

options.label: A continent crashing into South America
South America splitting apart along a rift
A plume of hot mantle rising beneath it
Ocean plates sinking under South America

items.explain: Subduction of the Nazca and Antarctic plates squeezes the western rim of the South American Plate and raises the range.

items.prompt: Dry conditions along the Chilean coast left parts of the subduction zone with little sediment to slick the sinking plate. What did that do to the Andes?
items.explain: With parts of the subduction zone starved of sediment, the sinking plate lacked a well lubricated surface, and contractional uplift along the coast sped up.

items.prompt: The Andes are the highest mountain range outside of which continent?
items.explain: No mountain range outside Asia is higher than the Andes.

items.prompt: The Andes sit along a belt of volcanic activity that rims which ocean?
items.explain: They are an orogenic belt on the Pacific Ring of Fire, which runs around the Pacific rim of the Americas and Asia.

items.prompt: Geographers group the Andean ranges into the Tropical Andes, the Dry Andes and the Wet Andes. What is this grouping based on?
items.explain: The three major divisions are drawn by climate, from tropical to dry to wet.
